cls: Integrin receptor antagonist / selective adhesion-molecule inhibitor (humanized anti-alpha-4 integrin monoclonal antibody)
pharm: A humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody against the alpha-4 subunit of integrins; it blocks leukocyte adhesion and migration into inflamed tissue (CNS, gut), reducing inflammation in multiple sclerosis and Crohn disease. It carries a boxed warning for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) and is available only through the TOUCH REMS program.
quick: 300 mg IV infusion over 1 hour every 4 weeks
Can cause fetal harm; neonatal thrombocytopenia/anemia reported - use only if clearly needed
Detected in breast milk; weigh benefit against risk
Clinically significant liver injury reported; monitor and stop if it occurs
Anti-JCV antibody, MRI, PML signs, liver function, infusion reactions
summary: Natalizumab (Tysabri) is a humanized monoclonal antibody against the alpha-4 integrin subunit, used as monotherapy for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis and for inducing/maintaining response in moderately-to-severely active Crohn disease refractory to conventional therapy or TNF-alpha inhibitors. It is given as a 300 mg IV infusion over 1 hour every 4 weeks. It carries a BOXED WARNING for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), a serious, often fatal opportunistic brain infection; risk rises with anti-JCV antibody positivity, treatment beyond 2 years, and prior immunosuppressant use. Because of this risk it is available only through the restricted TOUCH REMS program, with prescriber/patient certification and scheduled clinical evaluations. It is contraindicated in patients with current or prior PML and in those with hypersensitivity. Other risks include herpes encephalitis/meningitis, hepatotoxicity, hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis, and increased infection risk.
indications: Monotherapy for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis in adults (clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, active secondary progressive disease)

Inducing and maintaining clinical response and remission in adults with moderately-to-severely active Crohn disease with inadequate response/intolerance to conventional therapy and TNF-alpha inhibitors

dosage.d: 300 mg by intravenous infusion over approximately 1 hour
dosage.n: Monotherapy; dilute in 100 mL 0.9% sodium chloride; never give as IV push or bolus

dosage.d: 300 mg by intravenous infusion over approximately 1 hour
dosage.n: Discontinue if no therapeutic benefit by 12 weeks; do not combine with immunosuppressants or TNF inhibitors

dosage.d: Observe during infusion and for 1 hour afterward
dosage.t: First 12 infusions, then per clinical judgment

admin: Administer only through the TOUCH REMS program by certified prescribers/infusion sites
Dilute 300 mg in 100 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride; infuse over approximately 1 hour (~5 mg/minute) - never push or bolus
Use the diluted solution within 48 hours; allow refrigerated solution to reach room temperature before infusion
Observe the patient during and for 1 hour after each of the first 12 infusions for hypersensitivity
Do not co-administer other medications through the infusion set side ports
Obtain anti-JCV antibody status and baseline MRI; reassess for PML risk over time
moa: Natalizumab binds the alpha-4 subunit of alpha-4-beta-1 (VLA-4) and alpha-4-beta-7 integrins expressed on the surface of leukocytes (except neutrophils). This blocks the interaction of these integrins with their endothelial receptors VCAM-1 and MAdCAM-1, preventing adhesion and transmigration of leukocytes across the endothelium into inflamed parenchymal tissue. In multiple sclerosis this is thought to reduce leukocyte migration across the blood-brain barrier into the CNS; in Crohn disease it reduces leukocyte trafficking into inflamed gut. The same impairment of CNS immune surveillance underlies the increased risk of PML.

absolute: Current or prior progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML)
Known hypersensitivity to natalizumab (reactions range from urticaria to anaphylaxis)
relative: Anti-JCV antibody positivity (markedly increased PML risk)
Prior immunosuppressant use and treatment duration beyond 2 years (increased PML risk)
Concurrent immunosuppressants or TNF-alpha inhibitors (do not combine)
Active or chronic infection; immunocompromised state
History of clinically significant liver disease
monitor: Anti-JCV antibody status at baseline and periodically
Brain MRI at baseline and as indicated for PML surveillance
Clinical signs of PML (progressive weakness, vision/speech/cognitive changes)
Signs of infusion reactions and infections

preg: Natalizumab can cause fetal harm; neonatal thrombocytopenia and anemia have been reported with third-trimester exposure, and animal studies show immunologic/hematologic effects and reduced offspring survival at higher doses. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the risk. Neonates exposed in utero should have a CBC checked.
lact: Natalizumab is detected in human breast milk; the effects on the breastfed infant are unknown. A decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, taking into account the importance of treatment to the mother.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is described in labeling. As a monoclonal antibody it is not renally cleared in a manner requiring dose modification.
hepatic: Clinically significant liver injury, including cases requiring transplantation, has been reported, sometimes within days of the first dose. Monitor liver function and discontinue natalizumab if clinically significant liver injury occurs.

major: Other immunosuppressants/immunomodulators (e.g., 6-mercaptopurine, azathioprine, cyclosporine, methotrexate) - increased risk of infection including PML; contraindicated in combination in Crohn disease
TNF-alpha inhibitors - do not combine with natalizumab in Crohn disease
moderate: Chronic corticosteroids - taper off where possible in Crohn disease maintenance; combined immunosuppression raises infection risk
minor: Aminosalicylates may be continued in Crohn disease
interactions.diagnostics: Causes increases in circulating lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils, and a mild decrease in hemoglobin (mean ~0.6 g/dL); interpret CBC accordingly. Anti-natalizumab antibodies (~9-10%) can reduce efficacy and increase infusion reactions.

serious: Herpes encephalitis/meningitis and acute retinal necrosis
rare: Opportunistic infections such as PCP, aspergillosis, MAC (<1%)

monitoring: Anti-JCV antibody status at baseline and periodic retesting
Brain MRI at baseline and for PML surveillance
Neurologic status for PML symptoms at each visit
CBC (and CBC in neonates exposed in utero)
Hypersensitivity/infusion reactions during and after infusion
TOUCH REMS evaluations at 3, 6, and 12 months, then every 6 months
counsel: This medicine is given only through the TOUCH program - you will sign a consent form and be monitored regularly
It can rarely cause a serious brain infection called PML - tell your doctor at once about new weakness, clumsiness, vision changes, confusion, or personality changes
Report any fever, persistent infection, severe headache, or yellowing of the skin or eyes
Tell your care team if you feel itching, flushing, dizziness, or trouble breathing during the infusion
Do not take other immune-suppressing medicines with this drug unless your doctor directs
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding
Keep all scheduled appointments, including the every-4-week infusions and JCV antibody/MRI testing
pk: Pharmacologic effect on lymphocyte trafficking begins after first infusion; steady state ~16-24 weeks
Maximum serum concentration ~101-110 mcg/mL after a 300 mg infusion
Dosed every 4 weeks; trough ~10-29 mcg/mL at steady state
Refrigerate at 2-8 C; do not freeze; use diluted solution within 48 hours
pearls: BOXED WARNING: PML - risk rises with anti-JCV antibody positivity, >2 years of therapy, and prior immunosuppressant use
Available ONLY through the restricted TOUCH REMS program with mandatory prescriber/patient certification and scheduled evaluations
Contraindicated in current/prior PML; check anti-JCV antibody and baseline MRI before and during therapy
Do NOT combine with other immunosuppressants or TNF inhibitors - additive infection/PML risk
Watch for herpes encephalitis/meningitis, acute retinal necrosis, and rapid-onset hepatotoxicity
Anti-natalizumab antibodies develop in ~9-10% and can reduce efficacy and increase infusion reactions
missed: Natalizumab is given by a healthcare provider every 4 weeks. If an infusion appointment is missed, contact the infusion center to reschedule as soon as possible; do not attempt to self-administer. The provider will resume the every-4-week schedule.
overdose: Safety of doses above 300 mg has not been established and the maximum tolerated dose is unknown. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with monitoring for hypersensitivity, infection, and other adverse effects.
